title: Referrals
description: Understand GP referrals, why an appointment may be needed, referral validity, urgency and what information your specialist may require.
text: Patient Information Referrals Referrals are clinical documents and usually require an appointment so the doctor can confirm the reason, urgency and information the receiving specialist needs. Information for patients of Woolloongabba Medical Centre in Brisbane’s inner south. Specialist referrals Our current policy requires a consultation with a doctor to obtain a referral. A referral summarises the clinical reason for specialist review and provides information that helps the specialist understand the question being asked. How long a referral lasts Most GP referrals to a specialist are valid for 12 months from the specialist’s first consultation with you, unless the referral states a different period. A GP can also issue a longer or indefinite referral when ongoing specialist care is clinically appropriate. A new referral may still be needed for a new or unrelated condition. Referral renewals Do not wait until the day of a specialist appointment to discover that a referral has expired. If your specialist asks for a new referral, book with your GP in enough time for your care to be reviewed and the referral prepared. Why a valid referral matters A valid referral is generally required for Medicare to pay a specialist benefit. Without one, you may not receive the Medicare rebate for the specialist consultation. Referral information — healthdirect Appointment length An expired referral renewal may be suitable for a brief appointment, while a new referral generally requires a standard consultation. If the referral relates to a new or complex problem, a longer consultation may be more appropriate. Referral questions Why might a referral request need a consultation? A doctor may need to understand the clinical reason for referral, review relevant information and decide what type of referral is appropriate.
